features.summary: Run daily generation, bounded AI repair, validation, publication, and terminal summary ownership through one production entrypoint.
commands: corepack pnpm run daily:codex-pipeline -- --date YYYY-MM-DD --execute --publish --codex-bin codex.cmd
acceptance: A needs_ai_repair handoff is preflighted for kind, clean-root evidence realpaths, and direct launcher .tmp destination before Codex authors a contract and the same entrypoint resumes.
Automated repair is capped at five attempts and records attempted, authored, completed, edit count, terminal reason, and explicit failure state without treating a later block as recovery.
After a repair is applied, advisory review tasks remain evidence while only safe public-editorial tasks covering every error-severity path may enter the next write contract.

Every repair handoff carries the current matching error issues, issue.details, a deterministic blocking-signal fingerprint, and only the still-active paths; ready contracts cannot edit duplicate, cleared, or undeclared paths.

A later repair attempt continues only when its path/problem blocking-signal set is a strict subset of the last accepted set; unchanged, replaced, or expanded signals stall immediately, restore the last accepted report, preserve attempted evidence, and cannot re-enter through content_contract.

After the bounded repair budget is exhausted, advisory-only tasks cannot veto a safe editorial degradation; degraded sections and residual counts are derived only from error-covered public-editorial tasks.
Production repair uses read-only schema-constrained UTF-8 Codex output; the host validates and writes the contract, and a bounded timeout terminates the process tree with codex_timeout.

Claim verification overrides misleading source-level inference, quality and report_write share complete candidate coverage, and terminal summaries identify only the latest unresolved failure with non-empty error code, message, failures, and blocking evidence.

Source registry uses only source_group, content_tags, and credibility_tag for public classification. Legacy candidate/report source_level metadata remains open historical input and falls back only when projected into canonical public labels.

Report draft persists the merged discovery occurrence store before editorial selection, evidence caching, authoring, quality review, or report artifact writes; structural candidate errors may still block the legacy editorial artifact, but classification metadata never blocks the public occurrence stream.

Production Source Watch is connected only when the producer stage returns the exact artifact path/SHA-256 receipt, the dated producer and candidate pool have identical target_id:snapshot_fingerprint sets, and build proves the exact pool path plus SHA-256; zero inclusion remains a valid consumed state.
A live scheduler that still forces not_connected or consumed:false fails the workflow compatibility gate before release.

The project scheduler inventory contains exactly one automation, ai-2; its prompt reads the dated UTF-8 run summary with explicit PowerShell encoding and delegates health truth to it, while status:self-check remains a manual diagnostic rather than a second scheduled workflow.
stop_conditions: The entrypoint returns needs_ai_repair without exhausting or disabling its declared repair budget.
A repair prompt reads an initial or stale review after a newer post-attempt review exists, or a stalled loop authors another contract.
A repair attempt changes a cleared path, fails to strictly reduce blocking signals, or degrades the accepted checkpoint without rollback.
A legacy candidate/report classification value is rejected only because it is new, or editorial selection runs before the occurrence store is persisted.
Codex writes outside the bounded pipeline work directory.
A requested Source Watch path is reported as consumed without producer, fingerprint-lineage, persisted-pool, and build evidence.
The live automation prompt contradicts evidence-backed Source Watch summary semantics.
Any second D:\ai-daily-cn automation definition or publisher appears beside ai-2.
features.behavior: Keep the automation prompt thin while the repository-owned entrypoint closes repair/resume and terminal-state transitions.

features.summary: Persist every safely normalizable discovery occurrence before editorial selection and publish a source-grouped, paginated public signal stream without content admission gates.
commands: corepack pnpm run signals:write -- --date YYYY-MM-DD --input PATH
acceptance: Canonical occurrences are written from mergeDiscoveryPayloads().candidates before selectReportItems; editorial story/trend derivatives never masquerade as newly observed occurrences.

No content-admission gate exists in the public signal path: every record with a safe HTTP(S) material URL is retained, with title resolved from explicit text or a deterministic source/URL fallback; only a structurally unsafe individual record is isolated without blocking the remaining stream.

Duplicate URLs from different collectors or explicit observation_id values remain distinct occurrences and share only a cluster_id; repeated raw rows for the same observation_id are transparently coalesced with raw_record_count/coalesced_record_count, and transport pagination never becomes an item cap.
Credibility, content, source, health, and access metadata are labels and filters only and must not change membership or default chronology.
Unknown classification metadata falls back to other/pending_review instead of failing the pool, hiding the record, or changing its time order.

Observed candidates receive a persistent observation_id from explicit native provenance or stable collector/material/event provenance before selection; occurrence IDs are independent from candidate IDs, build timestamps, titles, summaries, and classification metadata, while canonical URL identity sorts query parameters before clustering.
Persisted and public URLs are canonical HTTP(S) values without credentials, fragments, tracking keys, or secret query parameters, and the same safety rule is enforced again when stores are loaded.
Future-dated source records remain visible with date_anomaly=future_relative_to_collection and use collected_at for default chronology instead of occupying the top of the stream.
Public projection exposes publisher and collected_via separately and omits candidate IDs, selection state, rejection reasons, scores, internal notes, and private paths.

The pre-PR2 public signal history is preserved once as immutable compressed occurrence stores with an exact SHA-256 manifest; production build and publish fail closed on any missing, extra, or changed shard and never read legacy candidate/report artifacts at runtime.
The index renders only non-empty source groups, and every occurrence appears exactly once across the page union for its group.
The complete signals tree is cross-file validated and swapped from a staged directory as one generation, so readers never receive mixed index/page generations.
stop_conditions: Any credibility, verification, authority, tier, quality, health, access, status, selection, or rejection value changes public membership or default order.
The signal stream is derived only after editorial selection, dedupes same-URL occurrences, or silently caps records.
Public artifacts expose internal editorial or operational fields.
A stale managed signal page survives a clean build, or cleanup can escape docs/signals.
features.behavior: Listen broadly, preserve occurrences, label uncertainty, and let readers filter without turning labels into hidden admission policy.

stop_conditions: Legacy post-selection candidate pools are described as canonical raw observations.
A preview or page size is interpreted as a total membership limit.

features.summary: Author prose for the optional legacy edited-report artifact from same-run evidence before its first formal quality review; reserve repair for exceptional residual defects.
acceptance: The single production entrypoint invokes one bounded, schema-constrained first-pass author after report_draft and before the first quality_review.

For the optional legacy edited report only, the plan proactively covers every existing story title/narrative, hot-blog summary, GitHub description, and Builder translation path, with source URLs, candidate references, or original text retained as private grounding hints; this authoring never controls public signal membership or chronology.
The host requires every declared legacy edited-report path exactly once and the existing text applier still rejects fact, URL, date, source, audit, missing, banned, or undeclared writes.

A complete contract becomes daily-report.authored.json for the first formal review without consuming the exceptional repair budget; Builder translation also synchronizes content through the existing applier.
An unavailable, invalid, incomplete, or partially rejected first-pass contract is recorded as fallback and the untouched deterministic draft proceeds through formal review and bounded repair.
Run summary reports first-pass enabled/status/attempted/task/edit/applied/rejected/reason/first_review_ok/exceptional_repair_task_count separately from automation_ai_repair.
translation_fidelity remains advisory and is never copied into a repair write contract unless a separate error-covered legacy-editorial task authorizes that exact path.
Exceptional repair consumes current review metrics and requirements, freezes resolved fields, and stops after the first non-improving attempt instead of spending the remaining numeric budget.
stop_conditions: First-pass authoring happens after quality_review or consumes repair budget.
A contract can omit a declared path, add an undeclared path, or partially apply while becoming the optional legacy edited-report input.
Fixture success is presented as proof that repair is already exceptional in production.
features.behavior: Generate the optional legacy edited-report artifact deterministically, author its declared prose once, judge once, and repair only exceptional error-covered residue without gating the source-first public stream.

stop_conditions: The first formal review still sees routine whole-lane Builder authoring tasks.

agentic_loop_policy.arbiter_boundary: Arbiters are read-only. They do not edit code, resolve conflicts, push, publish, merge, or make final user-facing decisions.
agentic_loop_policy.dispatch_boundary: Hooks and deterministic checks may request or validate loop evidence, but must not auto-dispatch delegated agents.
agentic_loop_policy.main_agent_responsibility: The main agent owns synthesis, user-visible decisions, integration, and final handoff.

loop_control_policy.control_plane: Loop Engineering decides when to continue, validate, interrupt, and record auditable action decisions.
loop_control_policy.default_behavior: Continue low-risk local work when scope, ownership, and validation are clear; interrupt when risk signals require human review.

context_engineering_policy.knowledge_layer: LLM Wiki keeps stable project knowledge in Markdown without duplicating raw sources or agent-native memory.
context_engineering_policy.write_policy: Initialize incrementally; require human confirmation before knowledge writes; preserve wiki content file-by-file during standard updates.
